MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  FEBRUARY 13, 2018

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order at
7:05 p.m. in the City Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by MAYOR HUFF.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Representatives from Boy Scout Troop 783 led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance. Following
the Pledge of Allegiance, the Boy Scouts introduced themselves and explained that Troop 783 has
one of the highest percentages of Scouts that achieve Eagle Scout and they are attending the
meeting as part of working toward a Communication Merit Badge which is required to achieve
the rank of Eagle Scout.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman.

City Council Members Absent:  None.

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

  NONE

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of
  the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by
  a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on
  separately.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE ITEMS A-F AS PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
FEBRUARY 13, 2018
 A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the City
  Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by title only.

  APPROVED.

  APPROVED.

C.  CITY COUNCIL ADJOURNED MINUTES OF JANUARY 30, 2018

  APPROVED.

D.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – JANUARY AND FEBRUARY 2018

  APPROVED WARRANTS 59527 THROUGH 59574 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $371,687.42; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 010118 THROUGH 010718;
  59252 (VOID); 59382 (VOID); 59405 THROUGH 59461; 59435 (VOID); 59491
  THROUGH 59518; AND 59517 (VOID) THE AMOUNT OF $348,831.90 FOR A
  GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $720,519.32 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

E.  COMMISSION/COMMITTEE ATTENDANCE REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 5, 2018

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

  NONE.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

  NONE.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PROPOSAL FROM WILLDAN ENGINEERING FOR PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING
  SERVICES FOR 2018 STREET RESURFACING PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the attached proposal from Willdan
  Engineering to provide professional engineering services for design, construction
  management and observation services for the 2018 Street Resurfacing Project in a not-
  to-exceed amount of $99,060.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
FEBRUARY 13, 2018
   Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material). He
  noted that the proposal includes Bluemound Road, Elmdale Drive, Rolingwood Drive
  Latigo Lane and Kingspine Road, which was inadvertently left out of the staff report; as
  well as a portion of Hawthorne Boulevard and a depression on Palos Verdes Drive North.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN it was noted that the linear footage for
  the project is approximately 8,000 linear feet. COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN expressed
  concern regarding the cost of the observation and inspection portion of the project.
  Assistant City Manager Grammer explained that an inspector would be on site every
  day through the project and the cost is consistent with previous proposals for similar
  projects and the amount of work required.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE PROPOSAL FROM WILLDAN
  ENGINEERING TO PROVIDE PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR
  DESIGN, CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT AND OBSERVATION SERVICES FOR
  THE 2018 RESURFACING PROJECT IN A NOT-TO-EXCEED AMOUNT OF
  $99,060.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

B.  EXTENSION OF MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING FOR USE OF PALOS VERDES
  PENINSULA HIGH SCHOOL POOL

  Recommendation: That the City Council enter into an Extension of Memorandum of
  Understanding between Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified School District and the City of
  Rolling Hills Estates for Use of Pool Facilities at Palos Verdes Peninsula High School
  through November 5, 2018.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda material) and
  provided an overview of the history of the City’s use of the facility and the City’s donation
  of Quimby funds in 2011 in the amount of $73,000. He noted that the short duration of
  the MOU extension is to coincide with termination of the MOU with the City of Rancho
  Palos Verdes and that the cities will be meeting with PVPUSD this spring to discuss a
  new MOU for use of the pool.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN, Community Services Director Clark
  commented that the PVPUSD is in the process of reviewing all of its facility rental rates
  including pools, sports fields, gyms and other school facilities.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN expressed concern that the PVPUSD is considering
  charging for use of the pool given that the City was the leader among Peninsula cities to
  contribute to a capital campaign for pool improvements and made a significant financial
  contribution with the understanding that the City’s residents would benefit from that
  contribution by having use of the pool facilities.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN noted that the current PVPUSD Board of Directors
  may need to be made aware of the history of this matter since many of them are new
  and may be unaware of what transpired previously.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
FEBRUARY 13, 2018
   In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Community Services Director Clark
  commented that the YMCA, who operates the City’s summer swim program, has
  information available on the number of participants in the program as well as
  evaluations of the program which continues to receive high marks.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL, Community Services Director Clark
  commented that the City has had an agreement for use of the facilities since 1969. City
  Attorney Davis further commented that it has been a voluntary agreement. Following
  brief discussion, staff was directed to research the terms of the agreement created after
  donation of Quimby funds to ensure that the terms continue to be met with a new MOU.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ENTER INTO AN EXTENSION OF MEMORANDUM OF
  UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN PALOS VERDES PENINSULA UNIFIED SCHOOL
  DISTRICT AND THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES FOR USE OF POOL
  FACILITIES AT PALOS VERDES PENINSULA HIGH SCHOOL THROUGH
  NOVEMBER 5, 2018.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  ORDINANCE NO. 720 ADDING CHAPTER 2.14 TO THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO THE OFFICE OF THE CITY ATTORNEY

  Recommendation: That the City Council waive full reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  720 adding Chapter 2.14 to the Rolling Hills Estates Municipal Code pertaining to the
  Office of the City Attorney.

  City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ noted a typographical error in Section 2.14.010(D) where
  the word “to” should be added between the words necessary and assist.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL WAIVE FULL READING AND ADOPT ORDINANCE NO.
  720 ADDING CHAPTER 2.14 TO THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL
  CODE PERTAINING TO THE OFFICE OF THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read Ordinance No. 720 by title only.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
FEBRUARY 13, 2018
 B.  PROPOSED AMENDED BUSINESS LICENSE TAX ORDINANCE

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Review the proposed ordinance as revised
  and draft resolution as presented; and 2) direct staff to prepare a the final ordinance
  and resolution for presentation to Council on February 27, 2018 at which time Council
  will act to call for the ordinance to be placed on the June 5, 2018 ballot and adopt the
  tax waiver for first year businesses.

  City Manager Prichard provided a staff report (as per agenda material). He stated that
  since the last meeting, the ad hoc committee and staff met with the Palos Verdes
  Peninsula Chamber of Commerce to discuss the issues raised and the proposed
  ordinance has been amended as a result of those discussions.

  MAYOR HUFF expressed her appreciation to the Chamber for their participation and
  input.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL also expressed her appreciation to the Chamber and noted
  that one change that resulted from the discussions is a recommendation that the
  business license tax be waived for the first year for new businesses and a minimum tax
  was put in place for some business categories. City Manager Prichard further reviewed
  the other changes as shown in the staff report including updates to the category
  affecting recreation businesses.

  Eileen Hupp, President and CEO, Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber of Commerce
  addressed the City Council expressing her appreciation to the City and staff for working
  collaboratively on this issue and expressed the Executive Board’s support of the need to
  update the ordinance. On behalf of the Chamber’s Executive Board she expressed the
  following concerns/suggestions with the ordinance as currently written: based on gross
  receipts, the ordinance will be challenging to administer and audit; it should be net tax
  positive; there should be more transparency with regard to comparing the proposed
  rates with the current fees; to lessen impact, the increase should be phased in over
  multiple years; and the rate being charged to residential care facilities should be
  reduced. She further commented that the Chamber would be open to holding one more
  meeting to discuss the issue.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that it may be good idea to hold one more
  meeting with the ad hoc committee, staff and the Chamber Executive Board and
  suggested that the Chamber propose alternative language where appropriate for Council
  to consider.

  Discussion ensued concerning the rate for residential care facilities, the “net tax
  positive” issue and phasing. City Manager Prichard explained the current process for
  calculating business license tax rates and commented that the proposed structure
  basing certain tax rates on gross receipts will be simpler to administer than the current
  application of gross receipts in the existing code.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
FEBRUARY 13, 2018
   MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL CONTINUE THIS MATTER TO THE FEBRUARY 27,
  2018 MEETING; AND DIRECT STAFF AND THE AD HOC COMMITTEE TO
  FURTHER ENGAGE THE CHAMBER OF COMMERCE EXECUTIVE BOARD TO
  ADDRESS THE ISSUES RAISED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR HUFF SO ORDERED.

C.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 19-17 – BLUEPRINCE SOFTWARE AGREEMENT FOR
  PLANNING AND CODE ENFORCEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve Planning Application PA-19-17,
  entering into an agreement between the City of Rolling Hills Estates and N. Harris
  Corporation (BluePrince Software), in the amount of $32,540, all to the satisfaction of
  the City Attorney.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  Ryan Frommel, N. Harris Corporation addressed the City Council to review a PowerPoint
  presentation providing background information on N. Harris Corporation and additional
  information on the how the BluePrince Software program will be implemented.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ regarding what happens to the City’s data
  if the contract is terminated, Mr. Frommel stated that the system can still run unless a
  major version update is issued; and because the City owns the data, it would remain
  available to the City.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL, Mr. Frommel commented that all of the
  City’s current information on parcels and other data will be uploaded into the system
  and staff will enter any new information as it come in.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL inquired as to the short warranty period. In response,
  Mr. Frommel commented that 90-day warranty is standard. City Attorney Davis
  commented that it was in response to the 90-day warranty that the City changed the
  termination rights and adjusted the payment section to a milestone based payment
  plan.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN, Mr. Frommel stated that N. Harris
  Corporation currently works with approximately 13 cities in California and the drop
  down menus configured in the program will be specific to the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN, Planning Director Wahba commented
  that the program will integrate all of the information into one system so that the
  Planning Department can provide more efficient service to the public.

  Also in response to COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN, Mr. Frommel commented that the
  program has the ability to integrate with the City’s financial software and the system
  can be set up to allow online payments. Discussion ensued concerning the process for
  setting up the online payment option. Mr. Frommel stated that they can integrate their
  system with the City’s online payment processing system.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
FEBRUARY 13, 2018
   COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION 19-17 AND
  ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES AND N. HARRIS CORPORATION (BLUEPRINCE SOFTWARE) IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $32,540.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  Recommendation: That the City Council provide direction to staff with regard to

  City Clerk Luce provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented that historically all Councilmembers have
  been listed as alternate delegates. COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN concurred.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE APPOINTMENT OF ALL
  COUNCILMEMBERS AS ALTERNATE DELEGATES TO SOUTH BAY CITIES
  COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR HUFF SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
FEBRUARY 13, 2018
 B.  CLEAN POWER ALLIANCE – SELECTION OF DEFAULT RENEWABLE RATE TIER
  (ZUCKERMAN)

  Recommendation: That the City Council discuss the various options and determine
  which default renewable rate tier would be most appropriate for the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN provided a report (as per agenda material). He noted
  that regardless of the decision the City makes, an individual user can select an alternate
  level of renewable energy based on the rate tiers available, or opt out of the Clean Power
  Alliance program completely. He further noted that if the City selects the 36% tier, it
  equates to a 2% difference in rates as compared to SCE. Discussion ensued concerning
  the rate tier options available.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL SELECT THE CLEAN POWER ALLIANCE DEFAULT
  RENEWABLE ENERGY RATE TIER AT 36%.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

At 9:07 p.m. MAYOR HUFF formally adjourned the open session portion of the City Council

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Douglas R. Prichard
City Clerk  City Manager
